Greensburg Terminal
Enterprise Terminals & Storage, LLC
Executive Summary
Risk Management Plan
EPA Identifier:  1000 0017 9282

Accidental Release Prevention and Response

At Enterprise, we are committed to operating and maintaining all of our processes (especially those using hazardous substances) in a safe and responsible manner.  We use a combination of accidental release prevention programs and emergency response planning programs to help ensure the safety of our employees and the public as well as protection of the environment.  This document provides a brief overview of the comprehensive risk management activities that we have designed and implemented, including:

* A description of our facility and use of substances regulated by EPA's RMP regulation
* An overview of our accidental release prevention programs
* A five-year accident history for accidental releases of chemicals regulated by EPA's RMP rule
* An overview of our emergency response program
* An overview of planned improvements at the facility to help prevent accidental chemical releases from occurring and adversely affecting our employees, the public, and the environment

Description of the Stationary Source and Regulated Substances

The Greensburg Terminal located in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania,  is owned by Enterprise Company, LP and is operated by ENTERPRISE.  

The Greensburg Terminal is a wholesale terminal facility for the storage and loading of propane.  The propane is received from a Enterprise underground pipeline and is stored in one of three above ground storage tanks, or in an underground storage cavern.  The stored propane is transferred from the storage bullet tanks or cavern into highway transport trucks for delivery of the propane to wholesale customers.  Ethyl mercaptan is added to the propane during the truck filling operation as an odorant to aid in propane leak detection.

The Greensburg Terminal was evaluated to determine if any regulated flammable or

toxic substances exceeded the threshold quantity.  Enterprise identified the regulated substances and quantities kept on site based on facility knowledge.  Propane and ethyl mercaptan are the only listed flammable substances which are stored above the threshold quantities at the Greensburg Terminal and are subject to regluation by the Risk Management Program regulation.  Butane is also stored at Greensburg Terminal in an underground storage cavern.  However, the butane cavern is not connected to the truck loading rack, only to a DOT-regulated pipeline   Consequently, the butane on site is kept only in storage incident to transportation, and is exempt from the RMP regulation.

The process is regulated by Federal OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 and 40 CFR Part 68.  We have entered the facility as an RMP Program Level 1 facility.

There are no toxic materials contained on site above the threshold limits.

General Accidental Release Prev

ention Program

The following is a summary of the accidental release prevention program in place at Greensburg Terminal.  The process at the facility is regulated by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Risk Management Program (RMP) regulation (Program 1).  Release prevention is provided through the use of written operating procedures, employee training in written procedures, including normal operation and emergency release procedures, and in the design of safety and release prevention equipment installed at the terminal site.  In addition, a written safety program designed to comply with all applicable OSHA safety performance regulations is strictly enforced at all Enterprise facilities, including the Greensburg Terminal facility.  As part of the Enterprise safety program, the facility utilizes procedures that are included in the Enterprise program, but may not specifically be required at non-PSM and/or RMP Program 1 facilities (e.g. Safe work practice training; safe work permitting and hot work permitting).

Universal Prevention Activities

The accident prevention program summarized previously is applied to all RMP covered processes at Greensburg Terminal.  Collectively, these prevention program activities help prevent potential accident scenarios that could be caused by equipment failures and human errors.

Specialized Safety Features

The Greensburg Terminal has safety features on many units to help contain/control a release, to quickly detect a release and reduce the consequence of a release.  The following types of safety features are used in the covered processes:

Release Detection

* Hydrocarbon (hazardous gas) detectors and alarms in the storage and loading areas
* Flame detection equipment in the storage and loading areas

Release Containment and Control

* Process relief valves that discharge to a flare to capture and incinerate episodic releases.
* Valves to permit isolation of the process (manual or automated).
* Automatic shu

tdown systems for specific process parameters (e.g., high flow).
* Secondary containment  to contain any release of liquid ethyl mercaptan..
* Redundant equipment and instrumentation where adviseable
* Dual mechanical seals with seal failure alarms installed on hydrocarbon liquid pumps, where feasible. 
* Storage tank internal emergency shut down and excess flow valves
* Atmospheric relief devices.

Release Mitigation

* Hand-held fire extinguishers 
* Personnel trained in emergency response and procedures.
* Personnel protective equipment (e.g., chemical protective clothing, flame retardant coveralls, hard hats, safety glasses, etc.)

Emergency Procedures Information

The Greensburg Terminal maintains a written emergency procedure, which is in place to protect worker and public safety as well as the environment.  The procedures are for the possibility of a fire or explosion if a flammable substance is accidentally released.  The procedures address notification of local emergency response agencies if a release occurs.  Employees receive training in emergency procedures.  The emergency procedure is updated when necessary based on modifications made to the terminal facilities. 

The overall emergency procedure program for the Greensburg Terminal is coordinated with the Hempfield Township Emergency Management Office (LEPC).  This coordination includes periodic meetings of the committee, which includes local emergency response officials, local government officials and industry representatives.  The Greensburg Terminal has around-the-clock communications capability w

ith appropriate LEPC officials and emergency response organizations (e.g., fire department).  This provides a means of notifying the public of an incident, if necessary, as well as facilitating quick response to an incident.  In addition to periodic meetings with members of the LEPC, the Greensburg Terminal conducts periodic site orientations and emergency response briefings for emergency response organizations.  The Greensburg Terminal also provides periodic refresher training to local emergency responders regarding the hazards of regulated substances in the terminal.

Planned Changes to Improve Safety

The Greensburg Terminal resolves all findings from PHAs, some of which result in modifications to the process.  Other recommendations for possible changes to improve safety come from periodic accident prevention program audits, incident investigations, or employee suggestions and recommendations.  The following changes are planned for implementation at the Greensburg Terminal.

* Planned upgrades to fire case PSV.
